settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: This path only runs for STORED entries with a data descriptor; supportsDataDescriptorFor() otherwise rejects the entry via UnsupportedZipFeatureException (ZipArchiveInputStream.java:775-780).

pushback() writes back through the PushbackInputStream sized to the buffer capacity, limiting how far back the code can unread; readDataDescriptor() re-reads a fixed structure and can throw on truncation.
The signature heuristic in bufferContainsSignature() predates the reviewed snapshot and is a known design trade-off, not clear evidence of a defect introduced here.
candidates.description: readStoredEntry() buffers the current STORED entry (used when the entry uses a data descriptor and allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor is enabled) by reading it into a ByteArrayOutputStream and scanning for the LFH/CFH/DD signatures. bufferContainsSignature() only inspects the first two bytes for the local/central header start and then confirms with a mix of LFH and CFH byte positions (buf[i]==LFH[0] && buf[i+1]==LFH[1] then either LFH[2]/LFH[3] or CFH[2]/CFH[3]); if a match is found the code computes readTooMuch = offset + lastRead - i - expectedDDLen, pushes the excess bytes back, writes the pre-signature prefix into the accumulator, and calls readDataDescriptor(). Because the loop bound is i < lastRead - 4 and the signature test uses fixed byte offsets, an entry whose payload contains bytes that look like a LFH/CFH/DD signature (or a malformed/absent descriptor) can make the scan terminate at a false position, producing an incorrect readTooMuch / ddLen-derived offset. That affects how many bytes are pushed back and where the stream resumes, which can corrupt subsequent entry parsing. No size limit is applied to the accumulated entry data in this path, so the accumulator grows with the attacker-declared entry content.
missing_evidence: Whether the false-positive branch can actually be triggered with a well-formed PushbackInputStream size (buf.capacity()) in practice was not verified by execution.
The exact upstream behaviour of bufferContainsSignature()/cacheBytesRead() for comparison (only the snapshot source was read).
No test or call path in the read spans demonstrated an end-to-end effect on later entry parsing.
preconditions: Archive is read via ZipArchiveInputStream with data descriptors in use (general purpose bit 3 set).
The STORED-with-data-descriptor path is reachable (allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor true, or entry method STORED with a descriptor).
Attacker controls entry payload bytes and/or the data descriptor field values.
candidates.title: ZipArchiveInputStream STORED-with-data-descriptor resynchronization relies on signature scanning of attacker-controlled content

counter_evidence: The constructor validates the first CFH signature and throws IOException when the central directory is empty/corrupt if the stream starts with a local file header (ZipFile.java:608-623), so obviously malformed directories are rejected.
Lengths are 16-bit (0xFFFF max) per record for name/extra/comment, bounding a single record's allocation; only the number of records is unbounded.
No code in the read spans performs extraction to disk, so no path-traversal (zip-slip) consequence is demonstrated.
candidates.description: populateFromCentralDirectory() positions at the central directory and loops while (sig == CFH_SIG), calling readCentralDirectoryEntry() for each record. readCentralDirectoryEntry() allocates byte arrays directly from the untrusted short fields read out of the record (fileNameLen, extraLen, commentLen), reads the corresponding bytes from the archive channel, sets sizes/crc from the record, and resolves Zip64 fields via setSizesAndOffsetFromZip64Extra(). Each parsed Entry is added to the entries list and name map. Nothing in the read loop bounds the number of entries or the cumulative memory used; a crafted archive can declare a very large number of central-directory records (each triggering object allocation and map insertion) or very large declared name/extra/comment lengths, which are allocated and read per record. The Zip64 path also promotes the attacker-supplied 64-bit compressed/uncompressed sizes and local-header offset into the entry via reparseCentralDirectoryData(), so downstream getInputStream()/getRawInputStream() create bounded streams from those values.
missing_evidence: No measurement was performed to determine whether the record count can be made large enough for a practical resource-exhaustion effect.
Behaviour of downstream consumers of the Zip64 offsets/sizes (getInputStream/getRawInputStream) with extreme values was not exercised.
Whether callers in this snapshot document/require their own limits was not confirmed (only ZipFile.java lines 1-799 were read; the remainder of the file was not available in this session).
preconditions: A caller opens an archive with ZipFile (constructor or SeekableByteChannel overload).
The archive's central directory contains attacker-controlled CFH records with large declared lengths and/or very many records.
The caller does not impose its own entry-count or memory budget.
candidates.title: ZipFile central-directory parsing appends entries with attacker-declared name/extra/comment lengths and Zip64 sizes without count or size limits
